title: Favorite banjoists and his banjos
summary: No single favorite banjoist; his first cheap banjo, his Vega now, Kimball's costly banjos.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Who would you say would be your very favorite banjo if you had to pick one of all times? If you ever heard, if you don't mind, I don't want to put you on the spot because it's one of the good.
Well, like I said, during that time, I don't know who could play the best banjo because all of them was good during them times. Just like I said, Irene Lee Hawley was an exceptional good man.
He's still living out in California. California.
Poucy was a good man, Sears was good. All of those dudes could play. All of them could play that banjo during them times.
What kind of a banjo did you have when you first got one? Remember the maker? Did it have a resonator and all? Or what type was it in those days?

Oh, it was an off-made. I bought it from Royal Island. I've forgotten the name, but the reason why I liked it, because they had red, white, and blue on it. It was kind of pretty, you know? And I wanted a pretty banjo, so I got that one.
George Danahar, your pinks is up there.
It was very cheap, but I just liked it because it was pretty to me. I got it, but it wasn't much of a banjo. In fact, it still isn't too good to win. The one I have now is really good.
What kind are you using now? I have a Viga now.
Yes, darling. And I got that Viga from Eddie Dorsey. Oh, yeah.
Yeah. We're just talking about it.
Now, my friend had two good banjos. Kimball. Kimball had banjos that cost quite the $500.
Yeah, I think Lawrence Marrero had an expensive one.
Yeah, he had an expensive one, too.
Gold, you know what? That's right. You know, I think Lil Harris still got his sand banjo. Yeah. Epiphone or Viga, whatever he had. I think he got Epiphone. Yeah, he still has it. Who's that?
